svg.title: Endpoint exemption and interior blockers
svg.desc: Three parallel grid rays compare an opaque observer endpoint that remains visible, an opaque interior terrain cell that blocks, and an opaque canonical edge that blocks.

g.text: Endpoint rule: the origin and target cells are excluded from terrain-opacity testing because they define the visibility question.opaque endpoint
Interior rule: every non-endpoint cell on the canonical supercover must satisfy the terrain transparency predicate.opaque interior
Boundary rule: only canonical edges formed by orthogonally adjacent cells in S.I.R.'s sampled line are tested for permeability.opaque boundary

rect.title: Opaque origin cell: deliberately ignored by cellTransparent at index zero, so it does not obstruct this line.
Opaque intermediate cell: present on the supercover and therefore sufficient to make lineVisible false.

line.title: Opaque canonical edge: this orthogonal sampled-cell boundary is present in opaqueEdges and blocks the line.

path.title: Passing ray: endpoint opacity is exempt, no intermediate terrain cell or sampled edge blocks, so the target remains visible.
Terrain-stopped ray: evaluation stops conceptually at the opaque intermediate supercover cell.
Edge-stopped ray: terrain is clear, but the sampled boundary predicate rejects the opaque edge.

g.text: Result: cellTransparent and edgesTransparent are both true.VISIBLE
Result: cellTransparent is false because an interior supercover cell is opaque.BLOCKED
Result: edgesTransparent is false because a sampled orthogonal boundary is opaque.BLOCKED

svg.text: The origin and target establish the question; only intermediate terrain and sampled orthogonal boundaries obstruct it.
